rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: Samura reports the Prophet's dream of punishments for abandoning Qur’an and prescribed prayer, spreading lies, adultery, and usury, alongside Abraham among children who died in fitra and forgiveness for mixed deeds; it depicts the Fire's judgment in 6:128.
rows.anchor: سَمُرَةُ بْنُ جُنْدَبٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِمَّا يُكْثِرُ أَنْ يَقُولَ لأَصْحَابِهِ

words: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's intercession on Judgment Day: those with even a grain of good and testimony to God's oneness emerge from Fire, while those whom the Quran has detained remain; this illustrates the verse's conditional permanence.
rows.anchor: عَنْ أَنَسٍ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: ٱلنَّارُ مَثْوَىٰكُمْ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's judgment scene: deeds govern passage over Hell's bridge, monotheists are rescued, and the last hell-dweller enters Paradise; Abu Sa'id recalls tenfold reward beyond Abu Hurayra's wording, illustrating the verse's Fire and divine mercy.
rows.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ النَّاسَ، قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ هَلْ نَرَى رَبَّنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
